```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lee_2024_colistin_elf"))$reference`
* ELF model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lee_2024_colistin_elf"))$description`
* Plasma model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lee_2024_colistin_plasma"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics13030258> (open access)
* Supplement (goodness-of-fit plots and VPCs, Figures S1-S4):
  <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/antibiotics13030258/s1>

Lee 2024 fitted two separate population PK models to colistin formed from
nebulized colistimethate sodium (CMS): one to epithelial lining fluid (ELF)
concentrations and one to plasma concentrations. The two were never linked
(CMS itself was not measured), so they are packaged as two independent model
files that share this vignette. Both are one-compartment models in which the
nebulized dose is absorbed through a Weibull-shaped, time-dependent first-order
rate:

$$\frac{dA_1}{dt} = -WB \cdot A_1, \qquad
WB = KAMAX \cdot \left(1 - e^{-(RA \cdot t)^{GAM}}\right), \qquad
\frac{dA_2}{dt} = WB \cdot A_1 - \frac{CL}{V} A_2$$

where $t$ is the time since the start of the current nebulization.

# Population

Twenty mechanically ventilated ICU adults (13 male, 7 female; mean age 68.9
years, mean weight 64.9 kg) with ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by
carbapenem-resistant *Acinetobacter baumannii* were enrolled at Haeundae Paik
Hospital, Busan, Republic of Korea, between August 2020 and December 2022
(Lee 2024 Table 1). Four were on ECMO and two on CRRT. Each patient received
CMS 0.9375 MIU (75 mg CMS, 28.125 mg colistin base activity, CBA) through a jet
nebulizer over 30 min every 6 h. ELF was sampled by bronchoalveolar lavage
before and 1, 3 and 5 h after the start of a nebulization (80 samples), and
plasma before and 1, 2, 3 and 5 h after (100 samples). All pre-dose
concentrations were zero (Lee 2024 Figure 1). No covariate was retained.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Lee_2024_colistin_elf")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing at its source. They are
collected here.

| Parameter | ELF model | Plasma model | Source |
|-----------|-----------|--------------|--------|
| `lcl` (CL/fm) | log(0.541) mL/min | log(26.3) mL/min | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (V/fm) | log(23.0) mL | log(67.4) L | Table 2 (V in mL for ELF, L for plasma, per the table footnote) |
| `lkamax` (KAMAX) | log(0.531) 1/h | log(1.20) 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lra` (RA) | fixed(log(2.16)) | fixed(log(2.70)) | Table 2, held constant (asterisk) |
| `lgam1` (GAM) | fixed(log(2.92)) | fixed(log(1.79)) | Table 2, held constant (asterisk) |
| `lfdepot` (F) | fixed(log(0.09)) | fixed(log(0.09)) | Section 4.5 and Discussion: bioavailability assumed 9% (Boisson 2014) |
| `etalcl` | 1.24^2 = 1.5376 | 1.96^2 = 3.8416 | Table 2 IIV CL/fm 124% / 196% |
| `etalvc` | 0.597^2 = 0.356409 | 1.11^2 = 1.2321 | Table 2 IIV V/fm 59.7% / 111% |
| `etalkamax` | 0.843^2 = 0.710649 | 0.643^2 = 0.413449 | Table 2 IIV KAMAX 84.3% / 64.3% |
| `etalra` | fixed(0.83^2) | fixed(0.83^2) | Table 2 IIV RA 83.0%, held constant |
| (IIV on GAM) | none | none | Table 2 IIV GAM 0, held constant |
| `propSd` | 0.271 | 0.185 | Table 2 proportional error 27.1% / 18.5% |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)` | | | Section 2.3, Eqs. (1) and (3) |
| Weibull rate `wb` | | | Section 2.3, Eq. (2) and the Table 2 footnote; see Assumptions |

# Units and dosing

Doses are entered in **mg of colistin base activity** (CBA) into `depot` as a
30-min infusion; 1 MIU of CMS = 80 mg CMS = 30 mg CBA, so the label dose of
75 mg CMS is 28.125 mg CBA. The model's fixed bioavailability of 9% applies to
that dose. Concentrations are total colistin in mg/L. Unbound concentrations
use the paper's assumed unbound fractions: 0.10 in ELF (Gkoufa 2022) and 0.34
in plasma (Mohamed 2012).

```{r units}
mod_elf <- readModelDb("Lee_2024_colistin_elf")
mod_pla <- readModelDb("Lee_2024_colistin_plasma")
cba_per_mg_cms <- 28.125 / 75
fu <- c(ELF = 0.10, Plasma = 0.34)
```

# Replicate Figure 4: typical-value profiles and steady-state fAUC24

Figure 4 of Lee 2024 shows typical-value unbound profiles for 25 to 125 mg CMS
every 6 h, with the steady-state fAUC24 printed in each legend.

```{r fig4-sim}
doses_cms <- c(25, 50, 75, 100, 125)
fig4_events <- function(dose_cms, n_doses) {
  rxode2::et(
    amt = dose_cms * cba_per_mg_cms, dur = 0.5, ii = 6,
    addl = n_doses - 1, cmt = "depot"
  ) |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, 6 * n_doses + 18, by = 0.05)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}
sim_fig4 <- function(mod, matrix, n_doses) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(doses_cms, function(d) {
    s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), fig4_events(d, n_doses))
    data.frame(time = s$time, Cc = s$Cc, dose = paste(d, "mg"), matrix = matrix)
  }))
}
fig4 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_fig4(mod_elf, "ELF", 4),
  sim_fig4(mod_pla, "Plasma", 24)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    free_ugL = Cc * 1000 * fu[matrix],
    dose = factor(dose, levels = paste(doses_cms, "mg"))
  )
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(fig4, aes(time, free_ugL, linetype = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~matrix, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Unbound colistin (ug/L)", linetype = "CMS dose qid",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Lee 2024 (typical patient)."
  )
```

The steady-state fAUC24 is four times the unbound AUC over the last 6-h
interval of 80 doses (20 days, about 16 plasma half-lives, so the residual
approach to steady state is below 0.01%). An `ss = 1` steady-state dose is not
used here: with the time-after-dose Weibull rate it settled about 0.9% low for
ELF.

```{r fig4-fauc}
fauc_ss <- function(mod, matrix, dose_cms, n_doses = 80) {
  t_last <- 6 * (n_doses - 1)
  ev <- rxode2::et(
    amt = dose_cms * cba_per_mg_cms, dur = 0.5, ii = 6, addl = n_doses - 1,
    cmt = "depot"
  ) |>
    rxode2::et(seq(t_last, t_last + 6, by = 0.01))
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev,
    rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
  ))
  cf <- s$Cc * 1000 * fu[[matrix]]
  4 * sum(diff(s$time) * (head(cf, -1) + tail(cf, -1)) / 2)
}
published_fauc <- tibble::tribble(
  ~matrix, ~dose_cms, ~published,
  "ELF", 125, 51987, "ELF", 100, 41590, "ELF", 75, 31192, "ELF", 50, 20795,
  "ELF", 25, 10397,
  "Plasma", 125, 3636, "Plasma", 100, 2909, "Plasma", 75, 2182,
  "Plasma", 50, 1454, "Plasma", 25, 727
)
fauc_tab <- published_fauc |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    simulated = fauc_ss(
      if (matrix == "ELF") mod_elf else mod_pla, matrix, dose_cms
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))
fauc_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = round(simulated), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 2)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Matrix" = matrix, "CMS dose qid (mg)" = dose_cms,
    "Published fAUC24 (ug*h/L)" = published,
    "Simulated fAUC24 (ug*h/L)" = simulated, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state fAUC24, simulated vs Lee 2024 Figure 4.")

# Deterministic: a typical-value solve against the paper's own typical-value
# numbers. The paper rounds to the unit, so agreement is to well under 0.5%;
# a dose-unit error (CMS instead of CBA) or a dropped bioavailability moves
# every row by a factor of 2.7 or 11.
stopifnot(max(abs(fauc_tab$pct_diff)) < 0.5)
```

The agreement pins three conventions at once: the dose is CBA, the 9%
bioavailability sits inside the model, and the unbound fractions are 0.10
(ELF) and 0.34 (plasma).

The first-dose ELF peak also identifies the form of the Weibull function (see
Assumptions). Digitised from Figure 4a, the 125 mg first-dose peak is about
3,800 ug/L unbound at about 1.55 h after the start of nebulization.

```{r fig4-peak}
peak_125 <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::filter(matrix == "ELF", dose == "125 mg", time <= 6) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(free_ugL, n = 1)
peak_125 |> dplyr::select(time, free_ugL)
stopifnot(
  abs(peak_125$free_ugL / 3800 - 1) < 0.10,
  peak_125$time > 1.4, peak_125$time < 1.75
)
```

# Replicate Figure 1 and the supplementary VPCs (Figures S3 and S4)

The study design (one 28.125 mg CBA dose over 30 min; ELF sampled at 1, 3 and
5 h; plasma at 1, 2, 3 and 5 h) is simulated with between-subject and residual
variability for 200 virtual patients per matrix.

```{r vpc-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240314)
n_sub <- 200
vpc_events <- function(obs_times) {
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = seq_len(n_sub), time = 0, amt = 28.125, dur = 0.5, evid = 1,
    cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = c(0, obs_times)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
vpc_elf <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_elf, vpc_events(c(1, 3, 5))) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(matrix = "ELF")
vpc_pla <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pla, vpc_events(c(1, 2, 3, 5))) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(matrix = "Plasma")
# Pre-dose (time 0) rows are kept for PKNCA below and left out of the
# percentile summaries.
vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(vpc_elf, vpc_pla) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dv_ugL = sim * 1000)

vpc_q <- vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(1, 2, 3, 5)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(matrix, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = quantile(dv_ugL, 0.10), p50 = median(dv_ugL),
    p90 = quantile(dv_ugL, 0.90), .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
observed_median <- tibble::tribble(
  ~matrix, ~time, ~obs_median,
  "ELF", 1, 11790, "ELF", 3, 15386, "ELF", 5, 8164,
  "Plasma", 1, 19.2, "Plasma", 2, 29.8, "Plasma", 3, 37.7, "Plasma", 5, 32.6
)
ggplot(vpc_q, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = obs_median), data = observed_median, colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~matrix, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of nebulization (h)", y = "Total colistin (ug/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Line and band: simulated median and 10th-90th percentiles.",
      "Blue: observed medians, Lee 2024 Figure 1."
    )
  )
```

```{r vpc-table}
# Simulated 10th / 50th / 90th percentiles digitised by the maintainers from
# the dashed lines of Figures S3b and S4b (semi-log panels).
digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~matrix, ~time, ~vpc_p10, ~vpc_p50, ~vpc_p90,
  "ELF", 1, 1580, 10500, 41100,
  "ELF", 3, 1300, 10500, 48500,
  "Plasma", 1, 2.1, 16.3, 108,
  "Plasma", 3, 3.6, 25.4, 142,
  "Plasma", 5, 2.3, 23.5, 134
)
cmp_vpc <- vpc_q |>
  dplyr::left_join(observed_median, by = c("matrix", "time")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(digitised, by = c("matrix", "time"))
cmp_vpc |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(p10, p50, p90), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Matrix" = matrix, "Time (h)" = time,
    "Sim P10" = p10, "Sim median" = p50, "Sim P90" = p90,
    "Observed median (Fig. 1)" = obs_median,
    "VPC P10 (Fig. S3/S4)" = vpc_p10, "VPC median (Fig. S3/S4)" = vpc_p50,
    "VPC P90 (Fig. S3/S4)" = vpc_p90
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated percentiles (ug/L) against Lee 2024.")

# Centre of a 200-subject cohort against the observed medians of 20 patients.
# The between-subject SD of log concentration is 1.0-1.5, so the sampling SE
# of a 200-subject median is about 0.1 on the log scale; the observed medians
# carry far more noise (n = 20). A factor of 2 still breaks on a dose-unit or
# bioavailability error, each of which moves every point 2.7- to 11-fold.
ratio <- cmp_vpc$p50 / cmp_vpc$obs_median
stopifnot(all(ratio > 0.5 & ratio < 2))
```

The simulated medians track the observed medians in both matrices. With 200
virtual patients the 10th and 90th percentiles are themselves noisy (roughly
+/-30% between draws), so they are shown for orientation; the comparison of the
IIV readings against these VPC percentiles was made on a 20,000-subject cohort
(see Assumptions). For plasma the authors' simulated 90th percentile sits
somewhat above the packaged model's under either reading.

# Replicate Table 3: individual steady-state fAUC24

Lee 2024 computed each patient's steady-state fAUC24 for 75 mg CMS every 6 h as
F x fu x daily dose / CL, using the post-hoc CL. The virtual cohort below uses
the same formula on simulated individual clearances.

```{r table3}
fauc_ind <- dplyr::bind_rows(vpc_elf, vpc_pla) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, matrix, cl) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fauc_mgh_L = 0.09 * fu[matrix] * 4 * 28.125 / cl) |>
  dplyr::group_by(matrix) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = median(fauc_mgh_L), q25 = quantile(fauc_mgh_L, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(fauc_mgh_L, 0.75), .groups = "drop"
  )
fauc_ind |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(median, q25, q75), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Matrix" = matrix, "Median (mg*h/L)" = median, "Q1" = q25, "Q3" = q75
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Simulated fAUC24. Lee 2024 Table 3 medians by clinical outcome:",
    "ELF 36.7 (cured) and 31.7 (failed); plasma 1.40 and 2.00 mg*h/L."
  ))
```

The simulated interquartile ranges are wider than the published ones because
the published values are post-hoc estimates, which shrink toward the typical
value when each patient contributes only three or four samples.

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run on the simulated observations at the study sampling times (with
residual error), per matrix, and compared against the observed median (IQR)
peak concentrations quoted in the Discussion: 21,950 (10,440-28,389) ug/L in ELF
and 43.51 (14.23-85.78) ug/L in plasma.

```{r pknca}
# Subjects drawn with a very high clearance decay to numerically zero by 5 h,
# where the integrator can undershoot by about its absolute tolerance. Check it
# is noise, then floor it so PKNCA sees no negative concentration.
stopifnot(all(vpc$dv_ugL >= -1e-6 * max(vpc$dv_ugL), na.rm = TRUE))
nca_conc <- vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(dv_ugL)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, treatment = matrix, time, Cc = pmax(dv_ugL, 0)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, id, time)
nca_dose <- dplyr::distinct(nca_conc, id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 28.125)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 5, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax,
  "ELF", 21950,
  "Plasma", 43.51
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/L", tmax = "h", auclast = "ug*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated vs. observed median peak concentration (single 75 mg CMS",
    "nebulization). * differs from the reference by more than 20%."
  )
)
```

```{r pknca-check}
cmax_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(published_nca, by = "treatment")
cmax_med
# Same factor-of-2 envelope and reasoning as the VPC medians above.
stopifnot(all(cmax_med$med / cmax_med$cmax > 0.5 & cmax_med$med / cmax_med$cmax < 2))
```

The simulated median peaks sit 10-20% below the observed medians in both
matrices (the plasma row can be flagged at the 20% line, depending on the
draw). The reference is the median of only 20 observed peaks, and the typical
model curves already sit slightly below the observed medians at 3 h in Figure 1
(ELF 15.2 vs 15.4 mg/L; plasma 34 vs 38 ug/L), so this is read as sampling
noise in the reference rather than a transcription error, which would move the
peak several-fold.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Form of the Weibull function.** Lee 2024 prints Eq. (2) in MathML as
  `KAMAX x (1 - (exp(-RA x time))^GAM)` and the Table 2 footnote as
  `KAMAX x (1 - exp(-RA x time)^GAM)`. Read literally, `(exp(-RA t))^GAM`
  equals `exp(-RA GAM t)`, in which RA and GAM collapse into one rate constant,
  which would make two separately reported, separately fixed parameters
  meaningless. The packaged models use the standard Weibull form
  `KAMAX x (1 - exp(-(RA x t)^GAM))` of the isavuconazole model the paper cites
  for it (Desai 2016, ref. 15; packaged as `Desai_2016_isavuconazole_secure`).
  The maintainers checked all three readings against Figure 4a: the standard
  form puts the first-dose ELF peak at 1.55 h, matching the figure; the literal
  form puts it at 1.30 h, and `(1 - exp(-RA t))^GAM` lowers the peak by 8%
  (to about 3,490 ug/L for 125 mg, against about 3,800 in the figure).
  `t` is the time since the start of the current nebulization (`tad(depot)`),
  which reproduces the identical repeated peaks of Figure 4a.
- **Bioavailability.** The paper says the 9% bioavailability (Boisson 2014)
  was assumed "to calculate the PK/PD index". It is inside the fitted model as
  well: the Figure 4 typical-value curves (and fAUC24 values) are reproduced
  exactly with F = 0.09, and these typical curves match the observed Figure 1
  medians. With F = 1 every prediction would be 11-fold too high.
- **Dose units.** The models take the dose in mg CBA. Figure 4 labels doses in
  mg CMS; the fAUC24 agreement above (which is exact only for CBA) pins the
  conversion 75 mg CMS = 28.125 mg CBA given in the Figure 1 caption.
- **Nebulization as a 30-min infusion into the depot.** The paper does not
  say how the 30-min nebulization was coded. Modelling it as a bolus into the
  depot changes the ELF peak by less than 1% and its timing by less than
  0.1 h, because the Weibull rate is still below a fifth of KAMAX at 15 min.
- **IIV scale.** Table 2 gives IIV as percentages under
  `theta_i = theta x exp(eta_i)` without saying how they were computed. The
  maintainers read them as `sqrt(omega^2) x 100` (the PsN convention; PsN was
  used for the bootstrap), giving `omega^2 = (pct/100)^2`. The alternative
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` gives markedly smaller variances for these large
  values (e.g. 1.58 instead of 3.84 for plasma CL). The maintainers simulated
  both readings (20,000 subjects each, with residual error) against the digitised dashed percentile lines of the
  supplementary VPCs: at 1 h in ELF the chosen reading gives 1,600 / 10,700 /
  41,700 ug/L against 1,580 / about 10,500 / 41,100 digitised, while
  `log(1 + CV^2)` gives 2,530 / 12,000 / 38,100.
- **IIV on GAM** is reported as 0 (held constant) and the packaged models carry
  no eta on it. IIV on RA is held at 83.0% in both models, as published.
- **Unbound concentrations** are not model outputs. The unbound fractions 0.10
  (ELF) and 0.34 (plasma) are the paper's assumptions and are applied in this
  vignette only.
- **CL and V units.** The `ini()` values keep the paper's units (CL in mL/min;
  V in mL for ELF and L for plasma); `model()` converts to L/h and L.
- No correction notice for Lee 2024 was found as of 2026-10-29.
